A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MM-FSS research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original MM-FSS segmentation results on S3DIS and ScanNet, ablations in Tables 3–6, and qualitative results.

after.justification: V3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, and qualitative evaluations reported in v1.

M1.justification: The shared backbone, IF/UF heads, MCF, MSF, TACC, losses, and two-stage training remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B. New Appendix C explains existing mechanisms without introducing components or changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use S3DIS and ScanNet with the same 1/2-way, 1/5-shot segmentation coverage, including transfer of ScanNet-pretrained features to S3DIS. No dataset, domain, or evaluated task scenario is added.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain AttMPTI, QGE, QGPA, COSeg, and COSeg† as comparators. The additional related-work citations in v3 are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 replaces 'randomly sampling' with 'uniformly sampling' while retaining the 0.02 m voxel grid and 20,480-point cap. The PDFs do not clarify whether this specifies the existing random sampling distribution or changes point selection. Other reported splits, metrics, training budgets, and evaluation episode counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix A retain the same module, modality, weighting, calibration, and VLM ablations, complexity analysis, and qualitative cases. Appendix C in v3 adds discussion rather than new analyses; the existing visual-results appendix becomes Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions report split-averaged mIoU without repeated-training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and the qualitative examples are retained. For example, both versions report MM-FSS mean 1-way 1-shot mIoU of 52.09% on S3DIS and 44.73% on ScanNet. No result entries, rankings, or findings change.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10) and Appendix B's projection and feature-alignment formulation remain unchanged apart from notation styling. The new MSF walkthrough restates existing equations; it adds no formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The multimodal FS-PCS novelty claim, MM-FSS contributions, and performance claims retain their scope. Although the abstract drops 'cost-free,' the introduction and conclusion retain the same setup, and the absence of additional annotation cost was already explained in v1.

C2.justification: New Appendix C elaborates why support-to-query knowledge transfer creates distinct multimodal challenges and how sparse 3D geometry complements dense 2D appearance. Its MSF discussion largely restates existing explanations. The limitations concerning dataset bias and environmental impact are relocated unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies constructing support sets by randomly sampling a target class and selecting point clouds containing it. This adds implementation documentation without stating an episode-construction change. Existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain, and the code hyperlink target is unchanged despite its revised label.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Zheng et al. (2024), Xiong et al. (2024), Huang et al. (2024), and Wu et al. (2023), while removing several general 3D references. Section 2 and Appendix C modestly expand the explanation of multimodal few-shot challenges; the central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V3 adds a discussion appendix, relocates the limitations paragraph, and renumbers the visual-results appendix from C to D. Local prose and cross-reference corrections, including Figure 5 column references, accompany added acknowledgments and expanded affiliations. The main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: All six tables and eight figures are retained. Figures 1–3 receive small caption or label edits, Table 1 clarifies its split-label explanation, and the first-page author layout is expanded. The figure panels and table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new discussion appendix makes the multimodal rationale clearer, Appendix B documents episode construction more explicitly, and corrected Figure 5 references make the existing analysis easier to follow. These provide modest gains in clarity and reproducibility while preserving the method and evidence. The random-versus-uniform sampling wording remains unresolved.
